mutation_families.transient-byte: Enumerate XOR deltas 1..255, replacements 0..255, and named AND/OR/stuck-bit mutations; include ineffective outcomes, stage and persistence explicitly.
mutation_families.persistent-byte: Same byte mutations, retained across uses; distinguish raw key/schedule mismatch from domain-local constant filtered-correct-output behavior.
mutation_families.transient-byte-or-local-skip: Transient byte families plus each declared single-domain local call/instruction skip. Capture, latch and authorization skips are not silently classified as S1.
mutation_families.single-bypass: One designated comparison, flag/register, branch or result-propagation bypass; exact emitted event and allowed values must be enumerated.
mutation_families.codeword-or-bypass: Each single bit/byte lifecycle or receipt mutation (L1), separately from a designated decision bypass (C1). Whole-codeword overwrite is not L1.
mutation_families.destination-or-bypass: Each destination-byte write mutation before final readback (D4), separately from a designated validation/status bypass (C1).

outcomes.reject-or-correct: No incorrect block may escape within the accepted model; effective faults must reject and retire. Ineffective correct-output cases remain outcome-leakage observations, not confidentiality passes.
outcomes.retained-mismatch: A mismatched retained key/schedule must be detected before release, with terminal retirement and cleanup; track the fault across subsequent uses.
outcomes.constant-filtered: Output comparison supplies integrity. Correct outputs under an ineffective domain-local constant fault may continue; persistent filtered-output leakage is accepted residual, not immediate-retirement evidence.
outcomes.bypass-obligation: Healthy data may remain correct after a lone bypass; all applicable DC1 pairings must still prevent faulty release. No single successful fixture qualifies this family.
outcomes.destination-obligation: Read back actual destination against both intact results before handoff. On failure retire; secret destination clears, public destination restores its old bytes.

dc1.rule: Enumerate every applicable data/skip site plus designated C1 event in temporal order, including import and later use. Record explicit compatibility reasoning; neither this candidate list nor a blind Cartesian product establishes completeness.

negative_controls: Correlated/shared source or constant corruption affecting both domains.
Correlated plaintext echo on encryption and ciphertext echo on decryption; equality remains valid AES output and is never rejected heuristically.
Mutation after the last check or failed trusted rollback/clearing; retain the documented final handoff window.
limitations: Source anchors locate candidate regions, not individual machine instructions or a frozen complete site inventory.
No artifact mapping or configuration is qualified. Existing runner paths are discovery references, not evidence receipts or current passes.
Expand each family into per-byte/per-stage/per-instruction cases and bind them to exact artifacts before freezing the inventory.
Preserve failed/unconfirmed runs, simulator limitations and analytic assumptions; do not infer coverage from test totals.
